## Question 1

```{r}
library(xml2)
library(stringr)

# Downloading the website
website <- xml2::read_html("https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=sars-cov-2")

# Finding the counts
counts <- xml2::xml_find_first(website, "//span[@class='value']")

# Turning it into text
counts <- as.character(counts)

# Extracting the data using regex
totalcount <- stringr::str_extract(counts, "[0-9,.]+")

# Removing commas/dots
totalcount <- gsub("[,.]", "", totalcount)

totalcount <- as.numeric(totalcount)
print(totalcount)
```


## Question 2

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines("C:/Users/caitl/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt", warn = FALSE)
# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row (indicating two blank lines)
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))
# replace any remaining "\n" symbols with spaces
abstracts <- gsub("\n", " ", abstracts)
# replace multiple spaces with single space
abstracts <- gsub(" +", " ", abstracts)
```

## Question 3

# Summary
    - To improve the results, I would:
• Normalize institution names (e.g., collapse “UCSD”, “UC San Diego”, and “University of California San Diego”).

• Remove department-level text such as “School of Medicine” or “Department of…”.

• Use a more restrictive regular expression that requires a comma or end-of-line after the institution name.

• Apply additional cleaning steps such as lowercasing and trimming whitespace.

These improvements would produce a more accurate and interpretable distribution of institutions.

```{r}
library(stringr)

institution <- str_extract_all(
  abstracts,
  "([A-Z][A-Za-z& ]+ University|University of [A-Z][A-Za-z& ]+|[A-Z][A-Za-z& ]+ Institute of [A-Za-z& ]+)"
)

institution <- unlist(institution)
table(institution)

sort(table(institution), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

```

## Question 4

```{r}
abstracts <- readLines("C:/Users/caitl/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt", warn = FALSE)
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))

library(stringr)

# Extract the whole first line
journal_raw <- str_extract(abstracts, "^[0-9]+\\.\\s*(.+)")

# Remove the number and period
journal <- sub("^[0-9]+\\.\\s*", "", journal_raw)


titles <- sapply(abstracts, function(x){
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[2]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Clean leftover line breaks
titles <- gsub("\n", " ", titles)
titles <- gsub(" +", " ", titles)

authors <- sapply(abstracts, function(x){
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[3]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

authors <- gsub("\n", " ", authors)
authors <- gsub(" +", " ", authors)

affiliations <- str_extract(
  abstracts,
  "(?s)(?<=Author information:\n).+?(?=\n\n)"
)

affiliations <- gsub("\n", " ", affiliations)
affiliations <- gsub(" +", " ", affiliations)

papers <- data.frame(
  journal = journal,
  title = titles,
  authors = authors,
  affiliations = affiliations,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(papers[1:5, ])

```
